name: toyota_2jz_ge
label: Toyota 2JZ-GE 3.0 L straight-six

sources.what: Australian Car Reviews technical article on the 2JZ-GE: block, head, valve sizes and lift, valve timing tables for non-VVT-i and VVT-i, intake (ACIS), exhaust, firing order. Detailed secondary source that reads like a digest of Toyota's new-car features documents; no primary citation given.
Online copy of the Toyota Supra (A80) repair manual service specifications for the 2JZ-GE: idle speed, cam lobe height, bore, journal diameters.
PDF copy of the 1997 Toyota Supra repair manual torque and service specifications; cross-check for idle speed.
Third-party spec page: power and torque ratings by version, firing order, valve and cam lobe dimensions. Secondary; figures agree with the two sources above where they overlap.
Wikipedia JZ article: variant overview and output range.

notes: Sourced: bore, stroke, compression ratio, firing order, valve diameters, valve lifts, valve events (3/50/53/3), idle, published output (lowest of the non-VVT-i ratings), two three-cylinder exhaust manifolds. The source does not say at what lift the valve events are measured; they are used as seat-to-seat figures (at_lift 0), which is an assumption. The firing order source does not say which end is cylinder 1; a 120-degree crank and manifolds for cylinders 1-3 and 4-6 are assumed. Estimated, not sourced: rod length (142 mm, seen only on aftermarket listings), redline, intake runner length, exhaust primary length, friction_scale and heat_q (tuned). Everything else is left to the derived defaults (runner and throttle diameters, plenum, pipes, mufflers, flywheel). Not modelled: the two-stage ACIS intake (one fixed runner length is used).

vehicle.name: Toyota Supra non-turbo five-speed (JZA80, US, 1993)
vehicle.notes: Curb weight (3260 lb, converted) and tyres are from The Auto Channel's period review of a 1993 non-turbo five-speed (220 hp at 5800 rpm). No Toyota source was found for the gear ratios (W58 box; Wikipedia) or the final drive (4.272 for 1993-96 US cars; a Supra tuner's differential table). No top speed found. wheel_radius_m is my calculation from the tyre size (half the rim diameter plus section width times aspect ratio): the unloaded radius; the loaded rolling radius is a few percent smaller.
